([[Avanhard Stadium (Luhansk)|Avanhard Stadium]], [[Luhansk]]) | capacity = 12,000 | owner = [[Yevhen Heller]] | chrtitle = Owner | chairman = Ihor Huz | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Viktor Skrypnyk]] | league = [[Ukrainian Premier League]] | season = [[2025–26 Ukrainian Premier League|2025–26]] | position = Ukrainian Premier League, 8th of 16 | website = {{url|https://fczorya.com/}} | current = 2026–27 FC Zorya Luhansk season | pattern_la1 = _zorya2627h | pattern_b1 = _zorya2627h | pattern_ra1 = _zorya2627h | pattern_sh1 = | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = | body1 = | rightarm1 = | shorts1 = FFFFFF | socks1 = FFFFFF | pattern_la2 = _zorya2627a | pattern_b2 = _zorya2627a | pattern_ra2 = _zorya2627a | pattern_sh2 = | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = | body2 = | rightarm2 = | shorts2 = 000000 | socks2 = 000000 | pattern_la3 = | pattern_b3 = | pattern_ra3 = | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = }} '''FC Zorya Luhansk''' ({{langx|uk|ФК «Зоря» Луганськ}} {{IPA|uk|zoˈrʲɑ lʊˈɦɑnʲsʲk|}}) is a [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[association football|football]] team based in the city of [[Luhansk]]. Due to the [[Russo-Ukrainian War]], after 2014 the team was forced to play its games at [[Slavutych-Arena]] in [[Zaporizhzhia]]. The modern team was established on 10 April 1964 by the [[Football Federation of the Soviet Union]], merging the October Revolution Plant ([[Luhanskteplovoz]]) sports club Zorya and the Luhansk regional branch of the "[[Trudovye Rezervy]]" sports society. In 1972, as Zaria Voroshilovgrad, the club became the first provincial Soviet club to win the [[Soviet Top League]] title. Today, they consider predecessor the football team of the Luhansk Steam Locomotive Plant (October Revolution Steam Locomotive Plant, today [[Luhanskteplovoz]]) that was established back in 1923, however due to poor performance of the factory team in the 1950s which played at republican level, the playing record of "Trudovye Rezervy" which played at all-Union level is also considered part of the club's history. It has been a flagman club in [[Luhansk Oblast]] and one of three Ukrainian football "teams of masters" that won the [[Soviet Top League]]. The name ''Zorya'' roughly means "dawn" in Ukrainian or more precisely the [[Red sky at morning|red skies]] phenomenon. [[File:Zorya Lugansk 2019.jpg|180px|thumb|right|FC Zorya Luhansk in 2019]]"}}
